what_the_eye_sees: Hero: a small winged creature statuette on a plain rectangular plinth on a band, like a trophy topper or a hood ornament. The creature is built from thin uniform tubes (limbs, neck, wing struts) with knobbed joints, so it reads as a wire armature, a toy robot or a stick-insect dragon. It does not read as a carved stone grotesque. The head is a small snout pointing right, with no gaping spout jaws, brow or horns visible at this size. The plinth is a plain box with what looks like a lettered name plaque, not a moulded Gothic parapet, cornice or corbel, and nothing on it says cathedral. Face: a tangle of rods and knobs lying along the band, unreadable. It could be a skeleton, an insect or machine parts. No head, wings or perch can be picked out. A jeweller would say 'dragon figurine on a pedestal ring' from the hero and 'I can't tell' from the face. Neither view says gargoyle or Gothic cathedral.
changes: Figure mass: replace the tube-and-knob armature with one hunched, solid sculpted body. Make the torso a heavy crouched lump about 1.5-2x its current thickness. Taper the limbs from thick haunches and shoulders to the claws, with no constant-diameter rods. Grow the head to about a third of the figure's length, with a heavy overhanging brow, short horns and pointed ears, and jaws gaping at least 2 mm with a channel running out through the mouth. Acceptance: at 300 px the hero silhouette shows a crouched beast with a big open-mouthed head, and no gaps between thin rods show background through the body.

Perch: make the plain box a Gothic parapet. Put a stepped cornice on top overhanging the block face by about 0.8-1.0 mm per step (two steps) and a tapering corbel below into the band. Remove the lettered plaque and put two blind quatrefoils or a small pointed-arch arcade in relief on the front face (finger-tip side), at least 0.4 mm deep. Acceptance: at 300 px the block shows a shadowed cornice line and pointed or foiled tracery, and nothing reads as text.

Posture and wings for the face camera: fold the wings tight along the back as two ribbed bat-wing membranes, not a splayed triangle plus loose struts. Have the forelimbs grip the cornice's front edge, and thrust the head and spout out past that edge by about 3 mm along the finger. Acceptance: in face-300 the outline reads as head, then hunched back with folded wings, then haunches, from fingertip to knuckle, with the spout clearly projecting beyond the parapet.
